text: Twenty-point-nine million barrels cross a single strait every day — nearly a fifth of the oil the world burns. Friday the twenty-seventh, Brent settles at seventy-two dollars, and everything looks calm.
Then it happens — on a Saturday, markets closed. Monday opens four fifty-two higher, six-point-two percent.
It spikes to eighty-two… then closes four under — whoever chased it bought the high.
You don't chase it — and you don't predict it.
The crisis picks the direction. The pattern picks the moment — and the price where you're wrong.
One day — entirely inside the day before.
The trigger — a close above the range, stop below it.
And it hits — two sessions later.
Then the premium unwinds — seventy by July.
That setup fired seventeen times — it reached target four.
And it isn't a one-off. July — another attack, another spike. The same pattern, four sessions later — target again.
Two in thirteen quiet — two in four after a shock. Its job is making being wrong cheap.
